full_judgment:
3. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Dhaka by order dated 1-12-03 sent the case records to one Md Sujayat Ullah, Metropolitan Magistrate, for a judicial inquiry who after receiving the case record held judicial inquiry and having examined 4 witnesses including the petitioner as complainant on 30-12-03 and 4-1-2004 sent the case record to the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on 15-1-04 stating that the allegations under sections 220, 116, 167, 500 and 501 of the Penal Code were prima facie proved against the accused persons namely, the respondent Nos. 5 and 6. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate thereupon transmitted the case record along with the judicial inquiry report to the respondent No. 4 Sessions Judge, Dhaka. The respondent No.4 then registered and numbered the case as Metropolitan Sessions Case No.39 of 2004 and thereafter on due hearing of the Advocate of the petitioner and perusal of the record of the case took cognisance of the offence against the respondent Nos.5 and 6 under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. 1947. Thereafter, the respondent No.4. Metropolitan Sessions Judge wrote a letter dated 4-3-04 to the government followed by another letter dated 9-3-04 for sanction. But the Office of the Hon'ble Prime Minister by a memo dated 22-4-04 addressed to the respondent No.4 (Metropolitan Sessions Judge Dhaka) declined to accord any sanction for prosecution against the respondent Nos.5 and 6 vide Annexure-D2. A copy of this letter dated 22-4-04 was also sent to the Director-General, Bureau of Anti-Corruption as well as to respondent No.5. From the aforesaid letter dated 22-4-04 it is found that the sanction was withheld being influenced by a memo dated 10-4-04 issued by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption. Against this backdrop, the petitioner filed an application before the respondent No.4, with a prayer for sending another letter to the Office of the Prime Minister seeking sanction against the respondent Nos.5 and 6. But the respondent No.4 by the memo dated 9-5-04 rejected the same without assigning any reason, Annexure-E. The petitioner then caused a Demand of Justice Notice dated 28-7-04 to be served on the Office of the Prime Minister for according sanction but without any success. Hence the present Writ petition and the Rule. 

 4. The respondent Nos.1, 5 and 6 entered appearance in the case and contested the Rule by filing separate affidavit-in- opposition asserting that the government in exercise of its discretion rightly withheld sanction for trial of the respondent Nos. 5 and 6, the impugned order withholding sanction was passed in accordance with law and is not liable to be questioned by the petitioner. 

 5. Mr Mahbubur Rahman, appearing for the petitioner, contends that since the respondent No.4. Metropolitan Sessions Judge was convinced on the basis of the petition of complaint and the report of the judicial inquiry made by Magistrate after having examined 4 witnesses that the prima facie case under section 409 of the Penal Code was made out against the respondent Nos. 5 and 6, the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 representing the Office of the Prime Minister illegally, malafide and arbitrarily withheld sanction. Mr Rahman also argues that the report of the judicial inquiry and other records of the case show that the respondent Nos. 5 and 6 did not commit the offence under section 409 of the Penal Code as the public servant but out of their private adventure. No sanction of the government was thereof necessary in commencing prosecution against the respondent Nos. 5 and 6. It is further urged in the alternative that since the present case is still pending before the respondent No.4, Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka there is no necessity of obtaining any sanction whatsoever from the government now for commencing prosecution against the respondent Nos.5 and 6, in view of section 28(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 inasmuch as the requirement of sanction has been altogether dispensed with for holding trial in corruption cases. 

 6. Mr Zaman Akhter Bulbul, the learned Assistant Attorney-General and Mr Hasan Faiz Siddique appearing with Mr Abul Hye for the respondents, submit that the government refused to accord sanction in due exercise of its discretionary power and accordingly, withholding of sanction cannot be questioned, It is also argued that since the alleged offence appears to have been committed in the District of Habiganj the government acting through the respondent Nos.1 and 2 legally withheld the sanction in the case. With regard to the contention raised by Mr Mahbubur Rahman that no sanction is now necessary for holding trial in view of section 28(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, it is contended that since the proceedings in the Metropolitan Special Case No.39 of 2004 were terminated for want of government sanction before the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 came into operation on 9-5-2004 section 28(2) has no application in the present case. 

 7. Now the question that falls for determination is, whether the withholding of sanction by the government, in the fact and circumstances obtaining in the case, is sustainable in law. 

 8. Prior to the coming into force of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 2004 it was a bar under section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 for the Special Judge to hold any trial against any public servant without obtaining any prior sanction from the government. The necessity of obtaining prior sanction was/is intended to provide protection to the public servant-against any frivolous prosecution for any offence committed by him as public servant. We have noted from the record that the petitioner filed the present case against the respondent Nos. 5 and 6 by filing a petition of complaint before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka under sections 220, 166, 167 and 500 of the Penal Code. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate caused a judicial inquiry to be held by referring the matter to another Metropolitan Magistrate to see whether there is a prima facie case made out by the petitioner. 

 9. Accordingly, judicial inquiry was held and in course or inquiry 4 witnesses were examined and an elaborate report was submitted stating that the allegations were prima facie correct. On receipt of this report the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate forwarded the case record including the inquiry report to the respondent No.4, Metropolitan Sessions Judge for taking necessary action. The Metropolitan Sessions Judge being prima facie satisfied took cognisance of the offence under section 409 or the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and sought for government sanction by Memo dated 4-3-2004 followed by another Memo dated 9-3-2004. The government thereafter by a letter dated 22-4-2004 refused to accord sanction and since this letter dated 22-4-2004 contained a reference of a Memo dated 10-4-2004 issued by the erstwhile Bureau of Anti-Corruption, the learned Advocate for the petitioner taking exception to this memo, dated 10-4-04 of the Office of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption emphatically submits that said memo not being a part of the record of the case ought not of have found place in the memo dated 22-4-04 refusing to accord. Sanction by the respondent No.2. He submits that the Office of the Prime Minister acting through the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 have committed a gross illegality in taking into consideration the aforesaid memo dated 10-4-04 of the Bureau or Anti- Corruption while taking decision to refuse sanction in this case. Mr Rahman has also contended that although the FIR was lodged on 22-12-02 but the amount of Taka 20 (twenty) lac seized from the possession of the petitioner by the respondent Nos.5 and 6 was not immediately produced before the Magistrate and as a result the said amount was not deposited with the treasury until 12-1-03 i.e. after a period of 20 days from the date of seizure. This fact along with other factum of the case as stated in the petition of complaint that respondent No.5 was inimical to the petitioner from before as respondent NO.5 often used to send his men to the petitioner for extorting money by way of gratification with the threat that if his demand was not met transport business of the petitioner will be crippled, go to show that the respondents committed the offence under section 409 of the Penal Code in their personal misadventure. Since the petitioner being a bonafide businessman refused to yield to this illegal demand respondent No.5 managed so many false criminal cases to be lodged against him. In the process of manufacturing false cases the respondent No.5 tried to extort money from the petitioner by means of coercion and intimidation by coming to the Dhaka office of this petitioner. 

 10. The case under consideration filed by the petitioner clearly shows that the respondent Nos.5 and 6 committed the offence under section 409 of the Penal Code in their personal capacity and not in their official capacity as a police officer and, as such, the sanction in the present ease were/are not at all necessary under section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. This view finds support in the case of Muhammad Riaz vs State PLD 1966 (WP) Lahore 379 wherein it was held that when a public servant commits offence in his private capacity no sanction of the government is required for his prosecution. In the case reported in PLD 1960 (SC) 351 it was similarly held that a public servant committing offence of cheating under section 420 of the Penal Code cannot be said to be acting in discharge of his official duty and no sanction was accordingly required. Similar principle was also upheld in the case reported in AIR 1969 SC 686 holding that beating or abusing a person by public servant to attain official object does not come within the purview of official duty and, as such, sanction was not necessary. 

 (২) এই আইনের অধীন ও উহার তফসিলে বর্ণিত অপরাধসমূহের বিচার ও আপীল নিষ্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (XL of 1958) এর section 6 4-4 sub-section (5) এবং sub-section (6) এর বিধান ব্যতীত অন্যান্য বিধানাবলী প্রযোজ্য হইবে। 

 The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (XL of 1958) এর কোন বিধান এই আইনের কোন বিধানের সহিত অসংগতিপূর্ন হইলে এই আইনের বিধান কার্যকর হইবে।
